summary: Implemented the provider-neutral renderer service and the real SkiaSharp drawing engine for the Jellyfin 12 plugin under ADR-009 and ADR-010. Added the immutable, verified-SHA-256 SourceImageInput descriptor (exact bytes, content type, oriented dimensions; no path/Jellyfin entity/provider DTO/credential/mutable image object); the minimal provider-neutral BadgeDefinition snapshot (selector, enabled flag, one bounded template) with the code-owned V1 default (all selectors enabled, '{value}' technical templates, fixed 'UPGRADE' status text) and BadgeDefinitionResolver that wraps the existing BadgeSelectorResolver and applies the bounded templates; RenderRequest (source, MediaIdentity, MediaMatch, optional BadgeMetadata, an immutable copy of the ordered definitions, output policy, cloned operational limits, secret-free configuration fingerprint, renderer/schema versions); and the bounded three-variant RenderResult (Rendered carrying a complete PNG artifact + content type + oriented dimensions + output SHA-256 + deterministic output fingerprint; PassThrough; Failed with exactly one safe reason code and never a partial artifact), exposed through IRenderer.RenderAsync. SkiaBadgeRenderer enforces the source byte/dimension and derived-output limits and the 4.5:1 palette contrast before decode, loads the embedded DejaVu Sans Bold bytes with no host-font fallback, decodes via SKCodec into sRGB, applies EXIF orientation to pixels before layout (verified with an injected orientation-6 JPEG), detects meaningful alpha, resolves the provider-neutral selection (never branching on provider kind), packs the bottom-left two-row/three-pill rail and the independent top-right status pill via the pure BadgeLayoutEngine (priority order, overflow to next row, further end-truncation, omission, safe-area clamping on short posters), and encodes a fixed-settings non-interlaced 8-bit PNG with RGB for opaque output and straight-alpha RGBA otherwise (canonical transparent-pixel RGB) while stripping all source metadata. Cancellation is checked at each documented checkpoint and any cancellation/exception discards partial output without mutating the source. Added BadgeGeometry, BadgeContrast/RgbColor, SourceOrientation/SourceOrientationExtensions, internal SkiaOrientation, and BadgeTextNormalizer.Shorten. The renderer is a pure library: no DI, configuration, provider, Jellyfin host API, filesystem, or artwork-publication wiring. The reviewer's F1 finding is resolved: BadgeLayoutEngine.FitToWidth now bounds the retained prefix to policy.MaximumScalarValues minus the ellipsis scalar count (and to less than the normalized text's scalar count), so the final visible pill text including '...' is always at most the ADR-009 24-scalar limit; two regression tests (including the reviewer's 16xU+0057 + 8xU+1671 reproduction) cover this and confirm further shortening still works. The optional F4 observation was also addressed with a trivial defensive list copy in RenderRequest (no behavior change). Default ./build.sh test is green at 514 passed / 10 environment-guarded skips / 524 total; with ARRTAGS_SKIA_COMPAT=1 and the pinned sysroot the full suite passes 524/524, including the nine real decode/draw/encode render cases.
validation: Read authoritative context before changing anything: AGENTS.md, GOALS.md, PLANS.md, docs/decisions.md ADR-009/ADR-010, docs/architecture.md section 9, docs/data-model.md sections 3.5-3.8, docs/research/skia-host-compatibility.md, all existing src/ArrTags/Rendering types, BadgeMetadata/MediaIdentity/MediaMatch/OperationalLimits, existing rendering tests, and docs/implementation/4.6 and 4.8 reports.

Inspected the pinned SkiaSharp 3.119.4 managed API surface with a throwaway reflection probe and executed a throwaway encode probe on the pinned native runtime: Rgb888x/Opaque encodes to PNG color type 2, Rgba8888/Premul to color type 6, 8-bit, zero interlace, transparent pixels decode to #00000000, two encodes are byte-identical, and chunks are IHDR/sBIT/sRGB/IDAT/IEND only.

Applied the reviewer F1 fix in src/ArrTags/Rendering/BadgeLayoutEngine.cs: FitToWidth now returns the already-normalized text when it fits, and otherwise bounds the retained scalar prefix to Math.Min(scalarCount - 1, policy.MaximumScalarValues - ellipsisScalarCount); when that bound is below one scalar the value is omitted. The final visible text, including the appended ellipsis, therefore cannot exceed policy.MaximumScalarValues.

Added regression tests in tests/ArrTags.Tests/BadgeLayoutTests.cs: WidthFittingKeepsFinalTextWithinTheAdr009ScalarLimit uses the reviewer's 24-scalar over-wide label (16xU+0057 + 8xU+1671) with a rune-width measure that fits only after dropping the wide trailing glyphs, and asserts the final pill text ends with '...', differs from the original, and has a scalar count within the ADR-009 24-scalar limit; WidthFittingStillShortensFurtherUnderMoreWidthPressure asserts the same label is shortened below 24 scalars when the width pressure increases. Before the fix the first case would have produced 26 scalars.

Applied the optional reviewer F4 observation in src/ArrTags/Rendering/RenderRequest.cs: the constructor now copies the caller's BadgeDefinition list into a read-only snapshot instead of storing the caller's reference. Behavior is unchanged (the resolver's inputs and ordering are identical).
Added the renderer service and drawing engine, then ran ./build.sh restore (locked mode) -> all projects up-to-date, no lock-file changes.

./build.sh test -> Passed: 514, Skipped: 10, Total: 524 (the previous 512/10/522 plus the two new layout regression tests). The ten skips are the environment-guarded Skia tests (the task 4.8 native round trip and the nine task 4.9 real render cases).

./build.sh package -> Build succeeded, 0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s); produced artifacts/ArrTags_0.1.0.0.zip (473,759 bytes) with the same package structure as before (ArrTags.dll, build.yaml, THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md, and the three licenses/ files).

Forced native renderer run: LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/tmp/opencode/jf/sysroot/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu FONTCONFIG_PATH=/tmp/opencode/jf/sysroot/etc/fonts XDG_DATA_DIRS=/tmp/opencode/jf/sysroot/usr/share ARRTAGS_SKIA_COMPAT=1 dotnet test tests/ArrTags.Tests/ArrTags.Tests.csproj --configuration Release --no-build --filter 'FullyQualifiedName~SkiaBadgeRendererRenderTests' -> Passed: 9, Failed: 0, Skipped: 0.
Forced native full-suite run with the same environment (no filter) -> Passed: 524, Failed: 0, Skipped: 0; the previous 522/522 forced result now holds at 524/524 with the two new tests.

The nine guarded render cases prove: opaque 600x900 source renders as a 600x900 image/png with PNG color type 2 and 8-bit non-interlaced IHDR and a 64-hex output hash/fingerprint; an alpha source renders as RGBA (color type 6), preserves source alpha outside badge pixels, and canonicalizes fully transparent pixels to #00000000; the technical rail and top-right status pill use the ADR-009 palette (#111827 / #B45309) and the status pill never appears top-left; the same request produces byte-identical PNGs, hashes, and fingerprints; rendering does not mutate the source bytes; unsupported bytes return a bounded Failed(UnsupportedInput); an injected EXIF orientation 6 JPEG is applied before layout (900x600 output from 600x900 encoded bytes) and a descriptor that ignores orientation is rejected as MalformedSource; and the output declares sRGB and contains no tIME/tEXt/zTXt/iTXt/eXIf chunks.

Unguarded tests prove pass-through (ineligible surface, non-Matched, no metadata, no displayable value, unavailable source), bounded Failed for source-byte/source-dimension/derived-output limits and low contrast, Failed(Cancelled), null-request guard, and the pure layout/contrast/definition/request/result/orientation behavior, including the new 24-scalar width-fitting regressions.

Inspected git status and git diff: no staged changes; only the intended task-4.9 source, test, and documentation files are modified/added; the pre-existing .opencode/agents/*.md modifications remain unstaged and untouched; no package manifest or lock file changed; no changes to RenderVersion.CurrentRendererVersion; no Jellyfin or ArrTags.Providers namespace usage in src/ArrTags/Rendering; no DI/host wiring.
Updated the task-4.9 documentation counts for the new totals: PLANS.md (514 passing + 10 guarded skips; 524 forced), README.md (514; 524 forced), and docs/changelog.md (514 + 10 = 524; 524 forced).
known_limitations: Embedded color-profile handling converts a supported profile to sRGB through Skia's decode into an sRGB destination and treats a profile-less input as sRGB, but it does not independently parse containers to detect a present-but-unparseable ICC/EXIF profile and fail closed on it; Skia treats such a profile as sRGB. Reviewer finding F2 accepted this as deferred to the ADR-010 PNG-contract tests in task 4.11, and it was not implemented now.
The orientation pixel transform is implemented for all eight EXIF orientations, but only identity and orientation 6 are exercised; full per-orientation golden coverage remains task 4.6/4.11.
RenderAsync is bounded synchronous CPU work wrapped in Task.FromResult; cancellation is cooperative at the documented checkpoints. The caller owns scheduling/concurrency.

Color-space wrappers are created per render and not explicitly disposed (the native sRGB color space is a shared Skia singleton); a static native-initialized field was deliberately avoided because it would force native load in unguarded environments.
The renderer proves same-process determinism; cross-process/cross-runtime byte determinism and pixel goldens are task 4.11.
The Jellyfin host source adapter, the renderer configuration model/fingerprint, DI/host wiring, and native-asset packaging are out of scope (Phase 5, tasks 4.10/4.6).
Reviewer finding F3 (null-request ArgumentNullException) was accepted as conventional and intentionally left unchanged.
